step_2_mechanism_candidates.name: Snare-compatible capture geometry (integrated retrieval ear/loop)
step_2_mechanism_candidates.core_mechanism: A pre-engineered capture loop, hook, or 'retrieval ear' on the proximal (venous) end of the eShunt that accepts a standard endovascular snare (e.g., Amplatz GooseNeck) for mechanical extraction.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.failure_mode_addressed: Migration, mechanical failure, malposition requiring repositioning.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.physical_principle: Standard endovascular snare-loop retrieval (well-established for IVC filters, central venous catheters, migrated coils).
step_2_mechanism_candidates.prior_art_saturation: HIGH — Lens LQ3 'ventriculoatrial shunt retrieval' returned 81 hits including direct case reports: Matsubara 2012 (transvenous retrieval of intracardiac VA shunt migration using snare); Aloddadi 2018 (endovascular retrieval of detached VA shunt into pulmonary artery). Scopus SQ2 'snare AND retrieval AND venous AND implant' returned 5 hits including 'Use of preformed nitinol snare' (1994) and 'Transcatheter Retrieval of Fractured IVC Filter Strut' (2016).
step_2_mechanism_candidates.white_space_for_eShunt: LOW — basic snare retrieval is standard-of-care for VA shunts, which are functionally analogous to eShunts. Cannot claim the basic mechanism.

step_2_mechanism_candidates.name: In-situ thrombolysis delivery channel (pharmacological rescue lumen)
step_2_mechanism_candidates.core_mechanism: A dedicated micro-lumen or side-port within the eShunt that delivers thrombolytic agent (tPA, urokinase) directly to the device's venous-end thrombus, dissolving clot without device removal.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.failure_mode_addressed: Thrombosis/occlusion of the shunt at the venous interface.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.physical_principle: Catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) — standard for DVT, pulmonary embolism, and occluded dialysis catheters.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.prior_art_saturation: MEDIUM — Lens LQ4 'thrombolysis implanted shunt' = 2403 hits; LQ5 'thrombolytic infusion CSF shunt' = 1186 hits. Scopus SQ3 'thrombolysis AND shunt AND occlusion' = 245 hits. Includes 'Continuous irrigation with thrombolytics for intraventricular hemorrhage' (Neurosurg Rev 2024) — analogous lumen-based thrombolytic delivery to CSF space.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.white_space_for_eShunt: MEDIUM — catheter-directed thrombolysis established; specific application as a venous-side rescue lumen for an eShunt is novel but may be considered obvious by §103.

step_2_mechanism_candidates.name: Electrothermal shape-memory alloy (SMA) release trigger
step_2_mechanism_candidates.core_mechanism: A nitinol (NiTi) anchoring element that, when heated by an external catheter or electrical current, transitions from martensite to austenite (soft/shape-recovering state), releasing the anchor from the vessel wall for retrieval.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth / endothelialization (where snare alone fails).
step_2_mechanism_candidates.physical_principle: NiTi shape-memory phase transition at ~30-40°C (austenite finish temperature, tunable by alloy composition).
step_2_mechanism_candidates.credibility: MEDIUM-HIGH — SMA release is established in IVC filter retrieval (OptEase, Celect, Denali). Specific application to eShunt raises thermal safety concerns (proximity to dura, brain, venous sinus endothelium).
step_2_mechanism_candidates.prior_art_saturation: MEDIUM — Lens LQ6 'nitinol shape memory implant release' = 1098 hits (mostly off-topic bioelectronics). Scopus SQ4 'nitinol AND shape-memory AND retrieval AND implant' = 4 hits (all materials science, off-topic). Google Patents GP3 returned EP2043551B1 (Novate Medical — vascular filter with shape-memory), US11690741B2 (Covidien — vascular remodeling device), US20110276091A1 (Gi Dynamics — Anchors with Biodegradable Constraints).
step_2_mechanism_candidates.white_space_for_eShunt: HIGH — SMA release exists for IVC filters but NOT for CSF-venous shunts. Thermal isolation to protect surrounding tissues is novel.

step_2_mechanism_candidates.name: Partially-bioresorbable anchor with timed retrieval window
step_2_mechanism_candidates.core_mechanism: A bioresorbable polymer (PLLA/PLGA/PCL) anchor section that loses mechanical strength via hydrolytic degradation over a defined period (e.g., 12-24 months), creating an 'easy retrieval window' when the non-resorbable shunt body is intact but the anchor releases with minimal mechanical force.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.failure_mode_addressed: Late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — provides a TIMED window of reduced adhesion without sacrificing shunt patency.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.physical_principle: Hydrolytic degradation of polyesters (PLLA, PLGA, PCL) — well-characterized bulk erosion kinetics.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.credibility: MEDIUM — bioresorbable stents (Abbott Absorb) are clinically validated. Concern: degradation timing must match clinical retrieval window. Cannot easily extend the patent term if the device must remain functional for years.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.prior_art_saturation: LOW-MEDIUM — Scopus SQ5 'bioresorbable AND stent AND retrieval' = 4 hits (Bioresorbable Electronic Implants 2019; PLLA/PLCL bioresorbable stents 2023). Google Patents GP4 returned V-Wave heart anchor (US20190328513A1) and Limflow devices for fluid flow (US10835367B2, US20220125572A1). NEAR-NEIGHBOR: US20110276091A1 (Gi Dynamics) 'Anchors with Biodegradable Constraints' — REQUIRES passage-level review.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.white_space_for_eShunt: HIGH — bioresorbable stents are designed to be ABSORBED, not RETRIEVED. Using resorption as a TIMED RETRIEVAL TRIGGER for a non-resorbable shunt body is a distinct mechanism.

step_2_mechanism_candidates.name: Bidirectional flow-reversal flush (retrograde clearing)
step_2_mechanism_candidates.core_mechanism: An external pump + pressure differential inversion that temporarily drives venous blood backward through the shunt (venous → CSF) to dislodge obstructing debris/protein aggregates.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.failure_mode_addressed: Luminal obstruction (protein aggregates, debris) without device removal.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.credibility: MEDIUM-LOW — physiological concerns about backflow contamination of CSF with venous blood (infection risk, blood-CSF barrier breach, subarachnoid hemorrhage risk).
step_2_mechanism_candidates.prior_art_saturation: MEDIUM — Google Patents GP5 returned Silk Road Medical patents (EP3789069B1, US12128204B2, US12156960B2) on retrograde carotid arterial blood flow — DIRECT prior art for flow-reversal concept in endovascular context. Scopus SQ6 'flow reversal AND catheter AND clearing' = 1 hit.
step_2_mechanism_candidates.white_space_for_eShunt: LOW — basic mechanism saturated by Silk Road Medical; physiological safety concerns make this the weakest candidate.

attacks.attack_description: Snare-capture retrieval (M1) is the standard-of-care for migrated VA shunts, with extensive case-report literature (Matsubara 2012, Aloddadi 2018, plus 81 Lens hits on VA shunt retrieval). A PHOSITA would naturally use a snare for any endovascular shunt retrieval. Why is a complex SMA release mechanism needed?
attacks.defense: Snare-capture alone FAILS in late retrieval after tissue ingrowth — Matsubara 2012 explicitly notes 'rostral catheter segment partially remained because of tight adhesion.' SMA release provides a SECONDARY mechanism for adherent cases where snare cannot extract the device. M3_REFINED (thermal-isolated SMA release) specifically addresses the failure mode where snare alone is insufficient.
attacks.verdict: SURVIVED — but only because M3_REFINED addresses a distinct failure mode (late retrieval after adhesion) that M1 cannot.
attacks.follow_up_attack_identified: If snare fails for adherent cases, why not just use stronger traction or adjunctive balloon angioplasty (well-established techniques)? Need to demonstrate that SMA release is mechanically NECESSARY, not just convenient.

hostile_attacks_NOT_yet_executed: ATTACK_2: Tissue thermal injury — what if thermal isolation fails or thermal diffusion exceeds design envelope?
ATTACK_3: Inadvertent activation — what if body temperature, MRI heating, or diathermy triggers release unintentionally?
ATTACK_4: Obviousness from IVC filter prior art (EP2043551B1, US11690741B2) — applying known SMA release to a vascular implant
ATTACK_5: Manufacturing scalability — NiTi thermal-isolated anchor fabrication tolerances

step_5_first_attack.attack_name: Snare-capture is sufficient (use the strongest plausible alternative)
step_5_first_attack.attack_rationale: Per 'push the envelope' doctrine, the leading candidate must survive an attack by its strongest plausible alternative. For M3_REFINED (SMA release), the strongest alternative is M1 (snare-capture) because it is the established standard-of-care for VA shunt retrieval (Lens LQ3 = 81 hits, multiple case reports of successful snare retrieval of migrated VA shunts).
step_5_first_attack.attack_argument: A PHOSITA faced with the need to retrieve an eShunt would naturally use a standard endovascular snare (Amplatz GooseNeck, Indy snare) — exactly as is done for VA shunts today. The eShunt has a proximal venous end in the dural venous sinus, which is accessible via jugular venous access. Adding a complex SMA release mechanism (with thermal-isolation requirements, additional manufacturing steps, regulatory burden, and inadvertent-activation risk) is unnecessary engineering. The invention is therefore OBVIOUS in light of the established snare-retrieval practice for VA shunts.
step_5_first_attack.defense_argument: M1 fails for LATE RETRIEVAL after tissue ingrowth. The Lens LQ3 hit Matsubara 2012 explicitly notes 'the rostral catheter segment partially remained because of tight adhesion' — snare traction was insufficient to extract an adherent VA shunt catheter. The eShunt is intended as a long-term (potentially multi-year or lifelong) implant, making tissue ingrowth virtually guaranteed for any retrieval >12 months post-implant. SMA release provides a SECONDARY release mechanism for adherent cases. Furthermore, the M3_REFINED candidate adds thermal isolation that is specifically required for the eShunt's anatomical context (proximity to dura, brain, venous sinus endothelium) — a constraint not present in IVC filter SMA release.
step_5_first_attack.verdict: SURVIVED — M3_REFINED addresses a distinct failure mode (late retrieval after tissue ingrowth) that M1 cannot solve. However, the survival is CONDITIONAL on the demonstration that (a) tissue ingrowth is a real clinical problem for eShunts (not yet quantified), and (b) SMA release with thermal isolation is mechanically NECESSARY (not just convenient) for this use case.
step_5_first_attack.follow_up_attack_identified_for_V2: ATTACK_2: If snare fails for adherent cases, why not use stronger traction or adjunctive balloon angioplasty (well-established)? Need quantitative comparison of pull-force required with vs. without SMA activation, accounting for tissue-ingrowth adhesion forces (typical 1-5 N for vascular implants at 6+ months).
honest_negative_results_during_attack: M3 basic mechanism (SMA release for vascular implant) is NOT novel — Novate Medical (EP2043551B1) and Covidien (US11690741B2) hold prior art for vascular filters/remodeling devices.
M3_REFINED novelty depends entirely on the THERMAL ISOLATION element, which has not been passage-level audited against these prior-art patents.
If passage-level review shows that EP2043551B1 or US11690741B2 already teach thermal isolation for vascular implants, the M3_REFINED candidate would be DESTROYED and would need to be redesigned.
